claim: llm-d's EPP scores candidate pods with a weighted linear combination: final_score = prefix_score*3 + kv_utilization_score*2 + queue_score*2.
The EPP runs a fixed 4-step cycle per request: Discover, Filter, Score, Select.
quoted_support: The EPP runs a 4-step cycle for every request: Step 1 — Discover... Step 2 — Filter... Step 3 — Score... Step 4 — Select.

claim: Filters that restrict candidate pods to disaggregated roles (decode-filter, prefill-filter, encode-filter) key on the llm-d.ai/role Kubernetes label.
stance_target: coupling of EPP filters to k8s pod labels
quoted_support: decode-filter, prefill-filter, encode-filter — filter by llm-d.ai/role labels for disaggregated topologies

claim: The llm-d-kv-cache Indexer maintains a global near-real-time view of KV-cache block locality via a Read Path (EPP queries the index during scoring) and Write Path (vLLM pods emit KVEvents over ZMQ that update the index).
stance_target: KV-cache-aware routing requires an out-of-band event-driven index, not just pod polling
quoted_support: As vLLM pods create or evict KV-blocks, they emit KVEvents via ZMQ. The Event Subscriber consumes these events and updates the KV-Block Index in near-real-time.

claim: llm-d's cache-aware routing achieved 57x faster time-to-first-token and 2x throughput versus round-robin on 8 pods / 16 H100 GPUs.
scope_conditions: llm-d v0.6.0 well-lit path benchmark, 8 pods, 16 H100 GPUs
quoted_support: The result is dramatic — 57x faster time-to-first-token, 2x throughput, and near-elimination of tail latency on identical hardware.

claim: Load-aware scoring is necessary because prefix-only routing succeeds on only ~55% of requests at high QPS, while combining prefix + load scoring achieves 100% success rate and 5x lower inter-token latency at the same load.
stance_target: a non-pod router must combine cache-affinity with load/queue-depth signals, not cache-affinity alone
quoted_support: Without load-awareness, prefix-only routing succeeded on only ~55% of requests at high QPS. With the combined scorer: 100% success rate and 5x lower inter-token latency at the same load.

claim: Disaggregated P/D KV transfer in llm-d uses NIXL over InfiniBand/RoCE RDMA, with the default NIXL port changed to 5600 as of vLLM v0.15.1.
stance_target: P/D disaggregation transport mechanism and version-pinned API detail
quoted_support: KV cache is transferred between them via NIXL over InfiniBand/RoCE RDMA (default port 5600 since vLLM v0.15.1).
